newsitem.title: UK: "No diets" promise in glossy UK big women mag.
newsitem.headline: "No diets" promise in glossy UK big women mag.

text.p: A glossy women's magazine to be launched in Britain next week is promising no diets and no pictures of wafer-thin models.
With the slogan "curves, cleavage and confidence" Encore magazine is aimed at bigger women. Research shows that one third of British women wear size 16 (U.S. size 12) or over.
Encore is published by the Conde Nast stable whose trend-setting Vogue magazine was accused in June of using skeletal models and encouraging slimming disorders like anorexia in young girls.
Feminists have long maintained that the models favoured by the fashion industry damage the self-esteem of ordinary women.
Therapist Susie Orbach, author of "Fat is a feminist issue," said the new magazine could help challenge the notion that women have to be thin to be beautiful.
"This is one of the ways that a campaign can get going. We know we could change the way we see things if all the magazines promoted models who were size 18 (U.S. size 14).
"Within a month we would all find it extremely attractive," Orbach told BBC radio.
